4º de Primaria · Inglés

Questions with do and does

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

En español, para preguntar basta con cambiar la entonación: «¿Te gusta el chocolate?». ¿Funciona igual en inglés? ¿Se puede decir «You like chocolate?»

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

En inglés hace falta una palabra ayudante al principio: Do o Does. Decimos «Do you like chocolate?». Sin ella, la pregunta suena rara. Y la respuesta es corta: «Yes, I do» o «No, I don't».

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Interview with a zookeeper

The school magazine sent Lucas and Emma to the city zoo to interview Mrs Brown, a zookeeper.

Lucas: Good morning, Mrs Brown. Thank you for talking to us. What do you do at the zoo?

Mrs Brown: I look after the big cats: the lions, the tigers and the snow leopards.

Emma: Wow! What time do you start work?

Mrs Brown: I start at seven o'clock. First I clean the enclosures, then I prepare the food.

Lucas: What do the lions eat?

Mrs Brown: They eat meat: about seven kilos every day!

Emma: How many lions are there at the zoo?

Mrs Brown: There are five. The oldest is called Simba. He's fifteen.

Lucas: Which animal is your favourite?

Mrs Brown: The snow leopard, Luna. She's very shy, but she's beautiful.

Emma: Do you like your job?

Mrs Brown: Yes, I do! I love it.

Lucas: Why do you love it?

Mrs Brown: Because every day is different, and I help animals that are in danger.

Emma: Are you ever afraid of the tigers?

Mrs Brown: No, I'm not. But I'm always very careful!

Lucas and Emma: Thank you very much, Mrs Brown!

1. The helper word do

In English, questions in the present simple need a helper word at the beginning: do. Look: «You like pizza.» → «Do you like pizza?». The helper goes first, then the person, then the verb.

En castellano: en español no tenemos esta palabra; solo ponemos los signos ¿? y cambiamos la voz. En inglés do no se traduce: es como una señal que avisa «¡atención, viene una pregunta!». Y recuerda que en inglés solo se escribe el signo de interrogación al final.

2. Do you…? Do they…?

We use Do with I, you, we and they: «Do you have a pet?», «Do we have English today?», «Do they live near the school?».

The verb stays in its normal form, the same as in the dictionary. These questions are perfect to know people: «Do you like football?», «Do you play an instrument?», «Do you speak French?». En castellano: «¿Tienes mascota?» se convierte en «Do you have a pet?». Fíjate en que el orden es distinto al español.

3. Does he…? Does she…?

With he, she and it the helper is Does: «Does your brother play basketball?», «Does she speak English?», «Does it rain a lot in London?».

Remember the rule of the -s: it goes to Does, so the verb doesn't have -s. We say «Does he play?», never «Does he plays?». It is the same trick as in negative sentences with doesn't. En castellano: la «s» viaja al ayudante y el verbo se queda limpio.

Vídeo: Do or does? Fun English song · ABC Buddies (YouTube) · 66 mil visualizaciones

4. Short answers

To answer a yes/no question we don't repeat the whole sentence. We use a short answer with the same helper: «Do you like cats?» – «Yes, I do.» / «No, I don't.»

With does: «Does your mum cook?» – «Yes, she does.» / «No, she doesn't.». En castellano: en español contestamos «sí» o «no» solos, pero en inglés es más educado añadir la persona y el ayudante. Decir solo «Yes» no está mal, aunque suena un poco seco.

5. Questions with be or with do?

In English, there are two main types of questions in the present. It's important to choose the right one:

  • When the sentence has the verb be (am, is, are), we just change the order: «You are tired.» → «Are you tired?» «She is ten.» → «Is she ten?»
  • When the sentence has any other verb, we use do / does: «You like pizza.» → «Do you like pizza?» «He plays chess.» → «Does he play chess?»

Never use do with be! We say «Are you happy?», not «Do you are happy?».

The short answers follow the same verb:

  • «Are you hungry?» → «Yes, I am.» / «No, I'm not.»
  • «Do you like apples?» → «Yes, I do.» / «No, I don't.»
  • «Is he your brother?» → «Yes, he is.»
  • «Does he live here?» → «Yes, he does.»

And can works like be: «Can you swim?» → «Yes, I can.»

A trick: look at the answer you expect. If it's an adjective or a place (tired, ten, at home), use be. If it's an action (play, eat, live), use do.

6. Question words

Some questions need more than yes or no. We use question words at the very beginning: What (qué), Where (dónde), When (cuándo), Who (quién), What time (a qué hora) and How (cómo).

The order is: question word + do/does + person + verb. «What do you eat for breakfast?», «Where does your cousin live?», «What time do you go to bed?». En castellano: es como poner primero el «¿qué?» o el «¿dónde?» y luego la pregunta normal con do.

7. Who, which, whose, how many, why

You already know what, where and when. Here are some more question words:

  • Who (quién): asks about people. «Who do you sit next to?» → «I sit next to Pablo.»
  • Which (cuál): asks to choose between a few options. «Which animal do you prefer: the lion or the tiger?»
  • Whose (de quién): asks about the owner. «Whose pencil case is this?» → «It's Marta's.»
  • How many (cuántos): asks about a number. «How many brothers do you have?» → «I have two.»
  • How old (cuántos años): «How old are you?» → «I'm nine.»
  • How often (con qué frecuencia): «How often do you go swimming?» → «Twice a week.»
  • Why (por qué): asks for a reason. «Why do you like summer?» The answer starts with because: «Because there's no school!»

Be careful with why and because: in Spanish both are por qué / porque, but in English they are different words.

Question words go at the beginning, before do or does: «Where do you live?» «What does she eat?» «How many pets do you have?»

Vídeo: Who, what, when, where, why · TheBazillions (YouTube) · 1,9 millones de visualizaciones

8. Building an open question

Let's build a question step by step. We want to know the place where Sara lives. 1. Question word: Where. 2. Sara = she, so the helper is does. 3. Person: Sara. 4. Verb, normal form: live. Result: «Where does Sara live?»

The answer is a full sentence, not a short answer: «She lives in Toledo». Now the -s comes back to the verb, because there is no helper. Consejo: el ayudante aparece en la pregunta y desaparece en la respuesta.

9. Questions about you

These are very useful questions to meet a new friend. Learn them by heart: «What's your name?», «How old are you?», «Where do you live?», «What do you like?», «Do you have any brothers or sisters?», «What's your favourite colour?».

Some of these questions use the verb to be (am, is, are) and don't need do: «How old are you?», «Where is your school?». En castellano: el verbo to be es especial y no necesita ayudante; se pone delante de la persona. Lo demás va con do o does.

10. Keep the conversation going

A good conversation is like a game of tennis: the ball goes from one person to the other. If you only answer «Yes» or «No», the game stops! Here are some tricks to keep the conversation going:

  • Add information to your answer: «Do you have pets?» → «Yes, I do. I've got a cat called Pipa. She's black and white.»
  • Ask the question back: «And you?» or «What about you?» → «Yes, I do. And you? Do you have pets?»
  • Show interest: «Really?» «That's interesting!» «Cool!» «Me too!» «Me neither.» (A mí tampoco.)
  • Ask a follow-up question (una pregunta más): «I play the violin.» → «Really? How often do you practise?» «Who is your teacher?»

Look at this example:

Ana: What do you do after school?
Max: I go to judo on Mondays and Wednesdays. What about you?
Ana: I go to music school. I play the piano.
Max: Cool! Do you like it?
Ana: Yes, I love it. I practise every day.
Max: Really? Every day? That's amazing!

See? Nobody stops the ball!

11. Reading: a pen friend

Read this email from Jack: «Hi Pablo! I'm Jack and I live in Manchester. Do you like sport? I love rugby. My sister Emma doesn't like sport, but she plays the violin. What do you do after school? I go swimming on Wednesdays. Does your school have a swimming pool? Mine doesn't. What time do you have lunch in Spain? We have lunch at twelve! Write soon, Jack.»

Find four questions in the text. Then answer them for Pablo: «Yes, I do», «I play basketball»…

12. Let's practise: class survey

Make a class survey (encuesta). Write five questions on a sheet: «Do you have a pet?», «Do you like vegetables?», «Do you play an instrument?», «What time do you get up?», «Where do you have lunch?». Ask five classmates and write their answers in a table.

At the end, tell the class one result with does or doesn't: «Marco has a pet. Inés doesn't have a pet». Consejo: cuando preguntes, mira a tu compañero, sonríe y di «Thank you!» al terminar.

13. Make a quiz

A quiz is a game of questions. It's a great way to practise questions with do and does! Here is a quiz about animals:

  1. Where do polar bears live? (a) In the Arctic (b) In Africa (c) In the jungle
  2. What do pandas eat? (a) Fish (b) Bamboo (c) Meat
  3. How many legs does a spider have? (a) Six (b) Eight (c) Ten
  4. Does a penguin fly? (a) Yes, it does. (b) No, it doesn't.
  5. Which animal sleeps upside down? (a) The bat (b) The owl (c) The cat
  6. Why do camels have humps? (a) To store fat (b) To carry children (c) To sleep

Answers: 1a, 2b, 3b, 4b, 5a, 6a.

To make your own quiz:

  • Choose a topic: animals, sports, your class, food, the planets…
  • Write six to eight questions. Use different question words.
  • Write three options for each question. Only one is correct!
  • Check your grammar: do with I, you, we, they and plural nouns; does with he, she, it and singular nouns.
  • Write the answers at the bottom.

Then swap quizzes with a partner. Who gets the most points?

Vídeo: The five W's song · Scratch Garden (YouTube) · 5,2 millones de visualizaciones

14. An imaginary interview

Imagine you can interview anybody in the world: a famous footballer, a singer, an astronaut, a character from a book… or even an animal! What questions would you ask?

Here is an imaginary interview with a dolphin:

Q: Where do you live?
A: I live in the Mediterranean Sea.
Q: What do you eat?
A: I eat fish and squid.
Q: How do you breathe?
A: I'm a mammal, so I breathe air. I go up to the surface.
Q: Do you have friends?
A: Yes, I do. I live in a group called a pod.
Q: What do you like doing?
A: I love jumping out of the water!
Q: Why do you whistle?
A: Because it's how we talk to each other.

Steps to write your interview:

  1. Choose your character.
  2. Find some information about him, her or it.
  3. Write six questions with different question words.
  4. Write the answers, as if you were the character.
  5. Act it out with a partner: one is the reporter and the other is the character!

Lo hacemos juntos

Make a question: «You speak English.»

  1. You → helper Do.
  2. Do + you + speak (verbo normal).

Resultado: Do you speak English?

Make a question: «Mario plays chess.»

  1. Mario = he → Does.
  2. El verbo pierde la -s: play.

Resultado: Does Mario play chess?

Ask about the time: «They have dinner at nine.»

  1. Palabra: What time.
  2. they → do.
  3. Verbo: have.

Resultado: What time do they have dinner?

Make a question: «She likes chocolate.»

  1. The verb is likes (not be): use does.
  2. Does + she + like (no -s).

Resultado: Does she like chocolate?

Make a question: «They are at the park.»

  1. The verb is be: change the order.
  2. Don't use do with be.

Resultado: Are they at the park?

Errores típicos

  • Preguntar sin ayudante: «You like pizza?» → «Do you like pizza?».
  • Usar Do con he/she: «Do she play?» → «Does she play?».
  • Dejar la -s tras Does: «Does he plays?» → «Does he play?».
  • Poner el signo ¿ al principio: en inglés solo va ? al final.
  • Responder con el verbo: «Yes, I like» → «Yes, I do».
  • Using do with be: «Do you are happy?».
  • Answering why without because.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Complete with Do or Does: «___ you like music?»

    Ver solución
    Do.

  2. Complete with Do or Does: «___ your dad cook?»

    Ver solución
    Does.

  3. Make a question: «They live in a flat.»

    Ver solución
    Do they live in a flat?

  4. Complete: ___ is your teacher? Mrs Ruiz.

    Ver solución
    Who

  5. Complete: ___ you hungry? Yes, I am.

    Ver solución
    Are

  6. Complete: ___ he play football? Yes, he does.

    Ver solución
    Does

  7. Write the answer word for why.

    Ver solución
    because

  8. How do you say «A mí también»?

    Ver solución
    Me too!

Nivel medio

  1. Make a question: «Lucía has a bike.»

    Ver solución
    Does Lucía have a bike?

  2. Short answer (yes): «Do you play tennis?»

    Ver solución
    Yes, I do.

  3. Short answer (no): «Does your cat sleep a lot?»

    Ver solución
    No, it doesn't.

  4. Translate: «¿Dónde vives?»

    Ver solución
    Where do you live?

  5. Complete: «What time ___ she get up?»

    Ver solución
    does.

  6. Complete: ___ pencil is this? It's Pau's.

    Ver solución
    Whose

  7. Make a question: You live in Madrid.

    Ver solución
    Do you live in Madrid?

  8. Make a question: He is nine.

    Ver solución
    Is he nine?

  9. Write a follow-up question for «I play the guitar».

    Ver solución
    For example: How often do you practise?

  10. Answer the quiz: How many legs does a spider have?

    Ver solución
    Eight.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Correct: «Does he likes apples?»

    Ver solución
    Does he like apples?

  2. Write two questions for a new friend.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Do you have any pets? What do you do after school?

  3. Write a six-question quiz about your class.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Write an imaginary interview with a famous person.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Have a two-minute conversation without stopping the ball.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Write five questions with be and five with do.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeThe class magazine interview

The class interviews people at school for an English magazine.

Pasos

  1. In pairs, choose somebody to interview: a teacher, the cook, an older pupil.
  2. Write eight questions with different question words and with be and do.
  3. Do the interview and take notes. Use follow-up questions.
  4. Write it up for the magazine with a photo.

Producto final: An interview for the class magazine.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses question words correctly.
  • Chooses be or do correctly.
  • Uses follow-up questions.
  • Writes the interview clearly.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • En la comida, cada uno hace una pregunta en inglés con Do o Does y los demás contestan con respuesta corta.
  • Preparad juntos cinco preguntas para un «amigo por carta» imaginario.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Interrogativas en presente simple con do y does; respuestas cortas; partículas interrogativas; intercambios orales para obtener información personal (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria).

  • Encuesta de clase con cinco preguntas y gráfico de resultados.
  • Juego «Find someone who…»: buscar compañeros que respondan «Yes, I do».
  • Entrevista por parejas a un personaje inventado.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Make yes/no questions with Do and Does (preguntas de sí o no)
  • Give short answers: Yes, I do / No, she doesn't
  • Ask open questions with what, where, when and what time
  • Interview a classmate about habits and likes
  • Use who, which, whose, how many and why
  • Choose between questions with be and questions with do
  • Keep a conversation going with follow-up questions
  • Write a quiz and an imaginary interview

Palabras clave

Do you…? · Does he…? · Yes, I do · No, I don't · short answer · What · Where · When · What time · question mark

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
